usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/scrapegraphai/api/crawl with JSON body {url, maxDepth?, maxPages?, maxLinksPerPage?, allowExternal?, includePatterns?, excludePatterns?, contentTypes?, fetchConfig?} — only url is required. Returns a job: {id, status, total, finished, pages}. Then poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/scrapegraphai/api/crawl/{id} (free) until status==="completed".
usage.outputShape: Initial paid POST: body.id (job id), body.status ("running"). Poll result GET /api/crawl/{id}: body.status ("completed"), body.pages[] each with {url, depth, links[], title, status, parentUrl, contentType, scrapeRefId}. Page content is referenced by scrapeRefId (fetch via the scrape endpoint for full content).
quirks: Async: the paid POST only QUEUES the crawl and returns {id, status:'running', pages:[]} — the result is NOT in the POST response.
Poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/scrapegraphai/api/crawl/{id} (no payment, returns 200 free) until body.status==='completed'; example.com crawl completed within the first poll.
Status sub-paths like /api/crawl/status/{id} or /api/crawl?id={id} return 404 — only /api/crawl/{id} works.
Each crawled page returns metadata + links + a scrapeRefId rather than inline page content; full page content lives behind the scrapeRefId.
Set maxPages/maxDepth/maxLinksPerPage low to bound cost/time; price is 'Varies' but the minimal 1-page crawl cost $0.01.
usage.guide: POST to https://x402.orth.sh/scrapegraphai/api/crawl with a JSON body containing at least {"url": "<seed-url>"}; add maxPages/maxDepth/maxLinksPerPage to bound the crawl (recommended to keep cost low). Pay via x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). The POST returns a job {id, status:"running"} — the crawl runs async. Then poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/scrapegraphai/api/crawl/{id} (free, no payment) every few seconds until body.status === "completed". Read results from body.pages[], where each entry gives the page url, discovered links[], title, contentType, and a scrapeRefId for the full scraped content.
